IMPLEMENTED.doc: the procedures the server registers. Anything outside the set is still called by the traces and must answer PROC_UNAVAIL, so the refusal is itself under test. PORTMAP_MINIMAL is an embedded portmapper that lets a client find the services but not change the table; PORTMAP_PROCS is the full rpcbind surface, which no server here implements.

SERVICES.doc: the portmap service table published at startup. DUMP returns it verbatim, so the ORDER is part of the contract.

UADDR_HOST.doc: the host half of the universal addresses rpcbind reports.

PM_SET_MUTATES.doc: PMAPPROC_SET/UNSET mutate the registry. Only meaningful when they are in IMPLEMENTED; a server publishing a fixed table does not register them at all.

EXPORTS.doc: the export list, in the order the server reports it. Two exports over one directory, so MNT has something to disambiguate and EXPORT has more than one row to order.

PATHS.doc: every path the traces may present to MOUNTPROC3_MNT, mapped to how it resolves. Closed universe: quint cannot do string surgery, so the resolution rules are enumerated.

MOUNT_HOST.doc: the hostname the server records in the mount table for the replay client. A property of the harness's transport rather than of the protocol -- every connection over one in-process transport reports one name.

NSM_MON_FROM_LOCKS.doc: the NSM monitor list is fed by NLM lock grants (a server monitoring its own lock holders) rather than by SM_MON (the classic statd).

NSM_ADDRS_DISTINCT.doc: monitored peers are distinguishable by source address. With one transport there is one peer address, so SM_NOTIFY's fallback match cannot tell monitored hosts apart.

NSM_INITIAL_STATE.doc: the state number a freshly started server reports.

NLM_UPGRADE_IS_NOOP.doc: a LOCK naming a range its own owner already holds is answered as an idempotent retry without re-evaluating the mode, so a shared-to-exclusive upgrade is a silent no-op.

NLM_SHARE_ENFORCED.doc: NLM DOS share reservations are enforced rather than merely accepted.

NLM_IN_GRACE.doc: the server sits in its post-restart grace window for the whole trace. A server whose lock state cannot survive a restart has nothing to reclaim and opens for business immediately.

NLM_BLOCKING.doc: blocking LOCK requests are served, so traces may issue them.

NLM_GRANT_CALLBACK_OBSERVABLE.doc: the out-of-band NLMPROC4_GRANTED callback that delivers a deferred blocking lock is observable by the replay client. It is addressed to the client's own lock manager, which a harness that is not a real lockd cannot receive; the lock is granted server-side either way.

NLM_CANCEL_MSG_CANCELS.doc: NLMPROC4_CANCEL_MSG withdraws a queued blocking request the way NLMPROC4_CANCEL does. RFC 1813 gives the two the same meaning; a server may nonetheless acknowledge the asynchronous form without acting on it.
